nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable function $f_0 : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ which is less than 1 and $\delta \in [0,1/2]$ such that \begin{align*} \forall P \in \mathcal{P}, \: P[f_0] &\le \delta \: , \\ \forall Q \in \mathcal{Q}, \: Q[f_0] &\ge 1 - \delta \: . \end{align*} Then \begin{align*} \eC(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{4\delta(1 - \delta)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: A separating [0,1]-valued test gives a lower bound (1/2) log 1/(4 delta(1-delta)) on the e-Chernoff divergence.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ be two sets of probability measures. Suppose that there exists a measurable function $f_0 : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+,\infty}$ which is less than 1 and $\delta \in [0,1/2]$ such that \begin{align*} \forall P \in \mathcal{P}, \: P[f_0] &\le \delta \: , \\ \forall Q \in \mathcal{Q}, \: Q[f_0] &\ge 1 - \delta \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: thm:echernoffDiv_lower_bound

nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_map_le} for the function $f_0$, we have \begin{align*} \eC(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \eC(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*} $f_0 \circ \mathcal{P} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\id] \le \delta\}$ and $f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\id] \ge 1 - \delta\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_anti}, we thus have \begin{align*} \eC(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \eC(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*} We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_bounded} to conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Data processing through f0, monotonicity in the sets, then the bounded-mean computation.

nodes.name: Data processing inequality through KL duality
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[\log f] &= \inf_{Q \in \mathcal{Q}_{\eff}} \KL(P, Q) \\ &\ge \inf_{Q \in \mathcal{Q}_{\eff}} \KL(\kappa \circ P, \kappa \circ Q) \\ &= \inf_{Q' \in \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\eff}} \KL(\kappa \circ P, Q') \\ &\ge \inf_{Q' \in (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\eff}} \KL(\kappa \circ P, Q') \\ &= \sup_{g \in \mathcal{E}_{\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}}} (\kappa \circ P)[\log g] \: . \end{align*} The first inequality is the data processing inequality for KL divergence. The second inequality comes from $\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\eff} \subseteq (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\eff}$, which we proved in Lemma~\ref{lem:effectiveSet_comp_subset}.
nodes.section: 4.2 Data processing inequality through KL duality
nodes.statement_short: Chain KL duality, KL data processing and the effective-set inclusion to get data processing for maximal log-utility.

nodes.name: Fix Q and use the E-variable bound Q[f] <= 1
nodes.statement: Let $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$. Since $f$ is an E-variable for $\mathcal{Q}$, we have $Q[f] \le 1$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.statement_short: Fix Q and use the E-variable bound Q[f] <= 1

nodes.name: Conclude the infinity set is Q-null
nodes.statement: Hence $Q[\{f = \infty\}] = 0$.
nodes.section: 2.1 Almost everywhere with respect to a set of measures
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the infinity set is Q-null

nodes.name: Easy direction from the inclusion of E-variables in randomized ones
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}} \subseteq \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}$, the left hand side is greater than or equal to the right hand side.
nodes.statement_short: Easy direction from the inclusion of E-variables in randomized ones

nodes.name: Jensen: bound the kernel's utility by utility of its mean
nodes.statement: For the other direction, let $\eta \in \mathcal{E}^R_{\mathcal{Q}}$ be a randomized E-variable. By concavity of $U$, \begin{align*} (\eta \circ P)[U] &= P[x \mapsto \eta(x)[U]] \le P[x \mapsto U(\eta(x)[\id])] \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Jensen: bound the kernel's utility by utility of its mean

nodes.name: The mean function is an E-variable, giving the reverse inequality
nodes.statement: The function $x \mapsto \eta(x)[\id]$ is a measurable function and belongs to $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
nodes.statement_short: The mean function is an E-variable, giving the reverse inequality

nodes.name: An E-variable for Q2 is one for Q1
nodes.statement: For $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2}$, we have $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}$ since $\mathcal{Q}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{Q}_2$.
nodes.statement_short: An E-variable for Q2 is one for Q1

nodes.name: Apply the numeraire property for Q1
nodes.statement: Then $P\left[f/f^*\right] \le 1$ by the numeraire property for $(P, \mathcal{Q}_1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the numeraire property for Q1

nodes.name: Conclude numeraire for Q2
nodes.statement: Thus $f^*$ is a numeraire for $(P, \mathcal{Q}_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude numeraire for Q2

nodes.name: Take a maximizing sequence and forward convex combinations converging a.s.
nodes.statement: Let $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of e-variables in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ such that $n \mapsto P[U(f_n)]$ is non-decreasing and $P[U(f_n)] \to \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)]$. Let $\tilde{f}_n$ be a sequence of measurable functions and let $\tilde{f} : \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}_{+, \infty}$, with $\tilde{f}_n \in \mathrm{conv}(f_n, f_{n+1}, \ldots)$ such that $\tilde{f}_n \to \tilde{f}$ $P$-almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: Take a maximizing sequence and forward convex combinations converging a.s.

nodes.name: Existence via the Komlos-type lemma
nodes.statement: That sequence exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_mem_conv_tendsto}.
nodes.statement_short: Existence via the Komlos-type lemma

nodes.name: Convex combinations remain E-variables
nodes.statement: By convexity of $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, $\tilde{f}_n \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ for all $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Convex combinations remain E-variables

nodes.name: Define f* as the liminf
nodes.statement: Let $f^* = \liminf_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n$. Note that $f^*$ is a measurable function such that $f^* = \tilde{f}$ $P$-almost surely.
nodes.statement_short: Define f* as the liminf

nodes.name: Fatou shows f* is an E-variable
nodes.statement: We have $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$ by an application of Fatou's lemma: for $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, \begin{align*} Q[f^*] = Q[\liminf_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n] \le \liminf_{n \to \infty} Q[\tilde{f}_n] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fatou shows f* is an E-variable

nodes.name: Concavity: utilities of convex combinations dominate
nodes.statement: By concavity of $U$ and the fact that $P[U(f_n)]$ is non-decreasing, we have \begin{align*} P[U(\tilde{f}_n)] &= P[U(\sum_{i=n}^{m_n} \lambda_{n,i} f_{i})] \ge \sum_{i=n}^{m_n} \lambda_{n,i} P[U(f_{i})] \ge P[U(f_n)] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Concavity: utilities of convex combinations dominate

nodes.name: Reverse Fatou with U bounded above gives f* attains at least the sup
nodes.statement: We also have $f^* = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n$ $P$-almost surely, hence by Fatou's lemma (using that $U$ is bounded from above), \begin{align*} P[U(f^*)] &= P[U(\limsup_{n \to \infty} \tilde{f}_n)] \ge \limsup_{n \to \infty} P[U(\tilde{f}_n)] \ge \limsup_{n \to \infty} P[U(f_n)] = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reverse Fatou with U bounded above gives f* attains at least the sup

nodes.name: Conclude equality
nodes.statement: Since $f^* \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$, we also have $P[U(f^*)] \le \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}} P[U(f)]$, which proves the equality.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude equality

nodes.name: Product of numeraires is an E-variable for the product family
nodes.statement: We first need to check that $E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1} E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$. For $Q_1 \in \mathcal{Q}_1$ and $Q_2 \in \mathcal{Q}_2$, we have \begin{align*} (Q_1 \times Q_2)\left[E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1} E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}\right] &= Q_1[E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}] Q_2[E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Product of numeraires is an E-variable for the product family

nodes.name: Fix f and rewrite the ratio by iterated integration
nodes.statement: Let's now check the numeraire property. Let $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$. Let $E^*_1 = E^*_{P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1}$ and $E^*_2 = E^*_{P_2, \mathcal{Q}_2}$. \begin{align*} (P_1 \times P_2)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_1 E^*_2} \right] &= P_1\left[\frac{1}{E_1^*}P_2\left[\frac{f}{E^*_2}\right] \right] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fix f and rewrite the ratio by iterated integration

nodes.name: Reduce to showing the inner integral is an E-variable for Q1
nodes.statement: If we can show that $x \mapsto P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1}$, then we can apply the definition of the numeraire for $(P_1, \mathcal{Q}_1)$ to obtain \begin{align*} (P_1 \times P_2)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_1 E^*_2} \right] &= P_1\left[\frac{1}{E_1^*}P_2\left[\frac{f}{E^*_2}\right] \right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing the inner integral is an E-variable for Q1

nodes.name: Fubini swaps integrals
nodes.statement: Let then $Q_1 \in \mathcal{Q}_1$. We want to show that $Q_1 \left[P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]\right] \le 1$. By Fubini's theorem, we have \begin{align*} Q_1 \left[P_2\left[\frac{f(x, \cdot)}{E^*_2}\right]\right] &= P_2\left[\frac{Q_1 \left[f(\cdot, y)\right]}{E^*_2}\right] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fubini swaps integrals

nodes.name: Reduce to a statement about Q2
nodes.statement: It now suffices to show that $y \mapsto Q_1 \left[f(\cdot, y)\right]$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a statement about Q2

nodes.name: Product-measure bound closes the argument
nodes.statement: Let $Q_2 \in \mathcal{Q}_2$. Then \begin{align*} Q_2\left[y \mapsto Q_1 \left[f(\cdot, y)\right]\right] = (Q_1 \times Q_2)\left[f\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} The last inequality holds since $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}_1 \times \mathcal{Q}_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Product-measure bound closes the argument

nodes.name: The marginal numeraire is an E-variable for Q composed with kappa
nodes.statement: First we need to show that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes \kappa}$. It is measurable and for $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \kappa)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] = Q\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The marginal numeraire is an E-variable for Q composed with kappa

nodes.name: Integrating against kappa gives an E-variable for Q
nodes.statement: We then check the numeraire condition. By Lemma~\ref{lem:eVar_integral_kernel}, $(x \mapsto \kappa(x)[f]) \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrating against kappa gives an E-variable for Q

nodes.name: Numeraire inequality for the composition product
nodes.statement: By the definition of the numeraire, we then have \begin{align*} P\left[\frac{\kappa(x)[f]}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*} That is, $(P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}\right] \le 1$ for all $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q}\otimes \kappa}$.
nodes.statement_short: Numeraire inequality for the composition product

nodes.name: Conclude it is the numeraire
nodes.statement: We have proved that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}$ is the numeraire for $(P \otimes \kappa, \mathcal{Q} \otimes \kappa)$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude it is the numeraire

nodes.name: Rewrite the ratio
nodes.statement: Let $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$. \begin{align*} (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] &= (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f/E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}{E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the ratio

nodes.name: Reduce to f/E* being an E-variable for P x H
nodes.statement: It suffices to show that $f/E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}$ is in $\mathcal{E}_{P \otimes H}$ to obtain that this is less than 1 by the numeraire property.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to f/E* being an E-variable for P x H

nodes.name: Use the same-kernel numeraire lemma and numeraire property
nodes.statement: Let $\eta \in H$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:numeraire_compProd_same_kernel}, \begin{align*} (P \otimes \eta) \left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}}\right] &= (P \otimes \eta) \left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P \otimes \eta, \mathcal{Q} \otimes \eta}}\right] \end{align*} and since $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$ it is in $\mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes \eta}$ and the numeraire property gives that this ratio is less than or equal to 1.
nodes.statement_short: Use the same-kernel numeraire lemma and numeraire property

nodes.name: Numeraire property holds
nodes.statement: We conclude that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}$ satisfies the numeraire property.
nodes.statement_short: Numeraire property holds

nodes.name: Jensen bound on the log-ratio
nodes.statement: We then have \begin{align*} (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\log \frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] &\le \log \left( (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\frac{f}{E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}}\right] \right) \le 0 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Jensen bound on the log-ratio

nodes.name: Take sup over f to get the log-utility bound
nodes.statement: We conclude that \begin{align*} P[\log f] \le P\left[\log E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}\right] + (P \otimes \kappa)\left[\log E^*_{P \otimes \kappa, P \otimes H}\right] \: . \end{align*} Taking the supremum over $f \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$, we obtain the desired inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Take sup over f to get the log-utility bound

nodes.name: Countable X case via the countable lemma
nodes.statement: The case of countable $\mathcal{X}$ is covered by Lemma~\ref{lem:exists_condNumeraire_of_countable}. (TODO: only for measurable singletons though) TODO: $\kappa \ll H$ hyp?
nodes.statement_short: Countable X case via the countable lemma

nodes.name: Countably generated Y: filtration by finite partitions (unfinished)
nodes.statement: Let's now consider the case where $\mathcal{Y}$ is countably generated. Then there exists a sequence of finer and finer partitions of $\mathcal{Y}$ into finitely many measurable sets $(A_{n,m})_{n \in \mathbb{N}, m \le 2^n}$ with $\mathcal{Y} = \bigcup_{m \le 2^n} A_{n,m}$ for all $n$, and such that the sigma-algebra on $\mathcal{Y}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra generated by the sets $A_{n,m}$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the filtration generated by the successive partitions, that is, $\mathcal{F}_n = \sigma(\{A_{n,m} \mid m \le 2^n\})$. TODO
nodes.statement_short: Countably generated Y: filtration by finite partitions (unfinished)

nodes.name: Unfold the definition of the effective set
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \{Q\}_{\eff} &= \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f, \ (\forall Q'' \in \{Q\}, Q''[f] \le 1) \implies Q'[f] \le 1\} \\ &= \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid \forall f, \ Q[f] \le 1 \implies Q'[f] \le 1\} \end{align*} This is the set of finite measures $\{Q' \mid Q' \le Q\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the definition of the effective set

nodes.name: Dominated measures belong
nodes.statement: Indeed, if $Q' \le Q$, then for all $f$ with $Q[f] \le 1$, $Q'[f] \le Q[f] \le 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Dominated measures belong

nodes.name: Test with scaled indicators to get domination
nodes.statement: Conversely, if $Q'$ is such that $(\forall f, \ Q[f] \le 1 \implies Q'[f] \le 1)$, then for any measurable set $A$, we can take the measurable function $f = Q(A)^{-1} \cdot \mathbb{I}_A$ (in which $0^{-1} = \infty$) to obtain $Q'(A) \le Q(A)$.
nodes.statement_short: Test with scaled indicators to get domination

nodes.name: Unfold both effective sets
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\eff} &= \{\kappa \circ Q \mid \forall f, (\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, Q'[f] \le 1) \implies Q[f] \le 1\} \\ (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\eff} &= \{R \mid \forall f, (\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, (\kappa \circ Q')[f] \le 1) \implies R[f] \le 1\} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Unfold both effective sets

nodes.name: Fix a measure and a test function
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa \circ Q \in \kappa \circ \mathcal{Q}_{\eff}$ and $f$ such that $\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, (\kappa \circ Q')[f] \le 1$. That is, $\forall Q' \in \mathcal{Q}, Q'[x \mapsto \kappa(x)[f]] \le 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a measure and a test function

nodes.name: Effective-set property of Q
nodes.statement: Then since $Q \in \mathcal{Q}_{\eff}$, we have $Q[x \mapsto \kappa(x)[f]] \le 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Effective-set property of Q

nodes.name: Conclude inclusion
nodes.statement: We have proved that $\kappa \circ Q \in (\kappa \circ \mathcal{Q})_{\eff}$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude inclusion

nodes.name: KL is minimised at Q among dominated measures
nodes.statement: Since $\KL$ is non-increasing in the second argument, \begin{align*} \inf_{Q' \le Q} \KL(P, Q') = \KL(P, Q) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: KL is minimised at Q among dominated measures

nodes.name: Identify the effective set of a singleton
nodes.statement: Since $\{Q\}_{\eff} = \{Q' \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X}) \mid Q' \le Q\}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:effectiveSet_singleton}), we obtained $\KL(P, Q) = \inf_{Q' \in \{Q\}_{\eff}} \KL(P, Q')$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the effective set of a singleton

nodes.name: Apply numeraire-KL duality
nodes.statement: By the duality of numeraire and $\KL$ divergence (Theorem~\ref{thm:eVar_KL_duality}), we have \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f] = \inf_{Q' \in \{Q\}_{\eff}} \KL(P, Q') = \KL(P, Q) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply numeraire-KL duality

nodes.name: Write KL as maximal log-utility
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:sup_eVar_singleton}, $\KL(P, Q) = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f]$.
nodes.statement_short: Write KL as maximal log-utility

nodes.name: Data-processing for maximal utility
nodes.statement: Then by Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_comp_le}, we have \begin{align*} \sup_{f \in \mathcal{E}_{\{Q\}}} P[\log f] &\ge \sup_{g \in \mathcal{E}_{\{\kappa \circ Q\}}} (\kappa \circ P)[\log g] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Data-processing for maximal utility

nodes.name: Identify the result as KL again
nodes.statement: And that last term is $\KL(\kappa \circ P, \kappa \circ Q)$, again by Lemma~\ref{lem:sup_eVar_singleton}.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the result as KL again

nodes.name: Non-a.c. R gives infinite utility
nodes.statement: If $R$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal{P}$, then $\mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) = \infty$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_eq_top_of_not_acSet}. Similarly, if $R$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to $\mathcal{Q}$, then $\mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) = \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-a.c. R gives infinite utility

nodes.name: Such R do not affect the infimum
nodes.statement: Hence, in both cases, the term $\alpha \mathcal{U_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q})}$ is infinite and does not contribute to the infimum defining $\eR_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$.
nodes.statement_short: Such R do not affect the infimum

nodes.name: One inequality from data processing; reduce to finite case
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_le}, we have $\eR_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) \le \eR_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$. Then either both sides are infinite and we are done, or the left hand side is finite.
nodes.statement_short: One inequality from data processing; reduce to finite case

nodes.name: Range of phi carries all measures
nodes.statement: Let $A = \phi(\mathcal{X}) \subseteq \mathcal{Y}$. Then for all $P \in \mathcal{P}$ and $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$, we have $\phi_* P(A^c) = 0$ and $\phi_* Q(A^c) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Range of phi carries all measures

nodes.name: Restrict the infimum to measures on A
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{cor:erenyiDiv_eq_iInf_support}, we can restrict the infimum defining $\eR_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q})$ to measures supported on $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the infimum to measures on A

nodes.name: Reparametrise measures on A as pushforwards
nodes.statement: Since $\phi$ is an embedding, every measure supported on $A$ is of the form $\phi_* R$ for some $R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$ (take $R = \phi^{-1}_* R'$, in which $\phi^{-1}$ is a partial inverse on the range of $\phi$). \begin{align*} \eR_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R' \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}), \: R'(A^c) = 0} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \phi_* \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \phi_* \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \phi_* \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \phi_* \mathcal{Q}) \right) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reparametrise measures on A as pushforwards

nodes.name: Embedding invariance of maximal utility concludes
nodes.statement: Using then Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_eq}, we get \begin{align*} \eR_\alpha(\phi_*\mathcal{P}, \phi_*\mathcal{Q}) &= \frac{1}{1 - \alpha} \inf_{R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})} \left( \alpha \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + (1 - \alpha) \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &= \eR_\alpha(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Embedding invariance of maximal utility concludes

nodes.name: Symmetrising R does not increase the objective by convexity
nodes.statement: First consider an arbitrary $R \in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{X})$. Then $R' = \frac{1}{2}(R + \phi_* R)$ satisfies $\phi_* R' = R'$ and by convexity (Lemma~\ref{lem:convex_maxUtility}) and Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_swap}, \begin{align*} \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R', \mathcal{Q}) &\le \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &\quad + \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{Q}) \right) \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P}) + \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrising R does not increase the objective by convexity

nodes.name: Restrict to phi-invariant R
nodes.statement: Hence we can restrict the infimum defining $\eR_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q})$ to measures $R$ such that $\phi_* R = R$.
nodes.statement_short: Restrict to phi-invariant R

nodes.name: For invariant R both utilities coincide
nodes.statement: For such measures, by Lemma~\ref{lem:maxUtility_map_swap}, $\mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{Q}) = \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\phi_* R, \mathcal{P}) = \mathcal{U}_{\log}(R, \mathcal{P})$ and we get the result.
nodes.statement_short: For invariant R both utilities coincide

nodes.name: Monotonicity gives one inequality
nodes.statement: First, by Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_anti}, since $B_{\le a} \subseteq \mathcal{D}_{\le a}$ and $B_{\ge b} \subseteq \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}$, we have \begin{align*} \eR_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le a}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}) &\le \eR_{1/2}(B_{\le a}, B_{\ge b}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity gives one inequality

nodes.name: Plan: data processing for the reverse inequality
nodes.statement: For the reverse inequality, we use the data processing inequality for e-Rényi divergence (Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_comp_le}).
nodes.statement_short: Plan: data processing for the reverse inequality

nodes.name: Bernoulli kernel maps mean-constrained sets to Bernoulli sets
nodes.statement: Let $\kappa : [0,1] \rightsquigarrow \{0,1\}$ be the Markov kernel defined by $\kappa(x) = \Ber(x)$ (the Bernoulli distribution with parameter $x$). Then for $P \in \mathcal{P}([0, 1])$, $\kappa \circ P$ is a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $P[\id]$, and thus $\kappa \circ \mathcal{D}_{\le a} = B_{\le a}$ and $\kappa \circ \mathcal{D}_{\ge b} = B_{\ge b}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bernoulli kernel maps mean-constrained sets to Bernoulli sets

nodes.name: Data processing gives the reverse inequality
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_comp_le}, \begin{align*} \eR_{1/2}(B_{\le a}, B_{\ge b}) &\le \eR_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le a}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge b}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Data processing gives the reverse inequality

nodes.name: Easy inclusion; write the constraint on f
nodes.statement: It is easy to check that the set on the right is included in $\mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}}$. The constraint on an e-variable $f$ for $B_{\le \delta}$ is that for all $p \le \delta$, \begin{align*} (1 - p) f(0) + p f(1) &\le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Easy inclusion; write the constraint on f

nodes.name: Extreme parameters give two constraints
nodes.statement: For $p=0$ and $p=\delta$ we thus get the two constraints \begin{align*} f(0) &\le 1 \: , \\ f(1) &\le 1 + \frac{1 - f(0)}{\delta}(1 - \delta) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Extreme parameters give two constraints

nodes.name: Define lambda and rewrite the constraint
nodes.statement: Let $\lambda = \frac{1 - f(0)}{\delta}$. Then $\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]$ and the second constraint can be rewritten as $f(1) \le 1 + \lambda (1 - \delta)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define lambda and rewrite the constraint

nodes.name: Check the constraint at 0
nodes.statement: We need to check that we also have $f(0) \le 1 + \lambda (0 - \delta)$, but the expression on the right is equal to $f(0)$ by definition of $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_short: Check the constraint at 0

nodes.name: Use the description of E-variables for bounded-mean Bernoullis
nodes.statement: We first compute $\mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}}$ with Lemma~\ref{lem:eVarSet_bernoulli_le}.
nodes.statement_short: Use the description of E-variables for bounded-mean Bernoullis

nodes.name: Reduce to a one-parameter maximisation
nodes.statement: We thus know that we can restrict the supremum over $f \in \mathcal{E}_{B_{\le \delta}}$ to functions of the form $f(x) = 1 + \lambda (x - \delta)$ for some $\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]$. \begin{align*} \mathcal{U}_{\log}(\Ber(1/2), B_{\le \delta}) &= \sup_{\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]} \frac{1}{2} \log (1 + \lambda (0 - \delta)) + \frac{1}{2} \log (1 + \lambda (1 - \delta)) \\ &= \frac{1}{2} \log \sup_{\lambda \in [0, \frac{1}{\delta}]} \left((1 - \lambda \delta)(1 + \lambda (1 - \delta))\right) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a one-parameter maximisation

nodes.name: Locate the maximiser
nodes.statement: The function $(1 - \lambda \delta)(1 + \lambda (1 - \delta))$ reaches its maximum at $\lambda^* = \frac{1 - 2\delta}{2\delta (1 - \delta)}$ which is in the interval $[0, \frac{1}{\delta}]$ since $\delta \in [0,1/2]$.
nodes.statement_short: Locate the maximiser

nodes.name: Evaluate the optimum
nodes.statement: Its value at the optimum is $\frac{1}{4 \delta (1 - \delta)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate the optimum

nodes.name: Push forward by f0 via data processing
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_map_le} for the function $f_0$, we have \begin{align*} \eR_{1/2}(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \eR_{1/2}(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Push forward by f0 via data processing

nodes.name: Pushforwards lie in the mean-constrained sets
nodes.statement: $f_0 \circ \mathcal{P} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\id] \le \delta\}$ and $f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\id] \ge 1 - \delta\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pushforwards lie in the mean-constrained sets

nodes.name: Monotonicity in the sets
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_anti}, we thus have \begin{align*} \eR_{1/2}(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \eR_{1/2}(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity in the sets

nodes.name: Evaluate via the bounded-mean lemma
nodes.statement: We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:erenyiDiv_bounded} to conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate via the bounded-mean lemma

nodes.name: Push forward by f0 via data processing
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_map_le} for the function $f_0$, we have \begin{align*} \eC(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \eC(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Push forward by f0 via data processing

nodes.name: Pushforwards lie in the mean-constrained sets
nodes.statement: $f_0 \circ \mathcal{P} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\id] \le \delta\}$ and $f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q} \subseteq \{P \in \mathcal{P}([0,1]) \mid P[\id] \ge 1 - \delta\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pushforwards lie in the mean-constrained sets

nodes.name: Monotonicity in the sets
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_anti}, we thus have \begin{align*} \eC(f_0 \circ \mathcal{P}, f_0 \circ \mathcal{Q}) &\ge \eC(\mathcal{D}_{\le \delta}, \mathcal{D}_{\ge 1 - \delta}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity in the sets

nodes.name: Evaluate via the bounded-mean lemma
nodes.statement: We now use Lemma~\ref{lem:echernoffDiv_bounded} to conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate via the bounded-mean lemma

nodes.name: Numeraire property
nodes.statement: $E^*_{\kappa, H}$ is a numeraire for $(P \otimes \kappa, \{P\} \otimes H)$, so we get the numeraire property as in Theorem~\ref{thm:numeraire_compProd_le}.
nodes.statement_short: Numeraire property as in the previous theorem

nodes.name: Membership in E-variables
nodes.statement: We now prove that $E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H} \in \mathcal{E}_{\mathcal{Q} \otimes H}$. Let $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$ and $\eta \in H$. \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \eta)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}\right] &= Q\left[x \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x) \eta(x)\left[E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}\right] \right] \: . \end{align*} For all $x$, $\eta(x)\left[E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}\right] \le 1$, since $E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}$ is an e-variable for $H(x)$. \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \eta)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}\right] &\le Q\left[x \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x)\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Show the product is an E-variable for Q x H

nodes.name: Disintegrate
nodes.statement: Let $Q \in \mathcal{Q}$ and $\eta \in H$. \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \eta)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}\right] &= Q\left[x \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x) \eta(x)\left[E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}\right] \right] \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the product iteratively

nodes.name: Bound inner integral
nodes.statement: For all $x$, $\eta(x)\left[E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}\right] \le 1$, since $E^*_{\kappa(x), H(x)}$ is an e-variable for $H(x)$. \begin{align*} (Q \otimes \eta)\left[E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}E^*_{\kappa, H}\right] &\le Q\left[x \mapsto E^*_{P, \mathcal{Q}}(x)\right] \le 1 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Inner integral at most 1 since conditional numeraire is an e-variable
